That points toward a 4-term law built from products of t- and v-factors and x- and v-factors. I ran out of tool calls before I could pin down the exact univariate forms.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    p=params
    term1 = p[0]*t**2/(1+p[1]*t**2)*v**2/(1+p[2]*v**2)
    term2 = p[3]*np.exp(-p[4]*x**2)*np.exp(-p[5]*v**2)
    term3 = p[6]*np.exp(-p[7]*x**2)*v**2/(1+p[8]*v**2)
    term4 = p[9]*t
    return term1+term2+term3+term4
